source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"This is the highest possible GCS total, reflecting maximum eye, verbal, and motor responses in all three testable domains overall.","B":"This is the lowest possible total GCS score, reflecting absent eye, verbal, and motor responses at the time of the neurologic assessment.","C":"This score is outside the valid GCS range and should be discarded because the scale permits only total scores from 3 through 14.","D":"This score by itself indicates severe traumatic brain injury and is an independent indication for immediate endotracheal intubation."}}
source_row.rationale: The Glasgow Coma Scale total ranges from 3 to 15, and 15 is the highest possible total when all components are testable. Option A is correct. Option B incorrectly calls 15 the lowest score. Option C falsely treats a valid score as outside the scale. Option D incorrectly interprets a normal maximum score as severe traumatic brain injury and an independent indication for intubation.
source_row.source_detail: Official Glasgow Coma Scale — What is GCS?/Derived indices and FAQ: eye, verbal, and motor components can yield a composite total from 3 to 15 when all components are testable; 15 is the highest possible total.
